skill.name: agent-management
skill.description: Designs and maintains Claude Code subagent configurations with scoped tools, model tiers, workflow phases, and template-aligned Markdown files.

security_audit.summary: Manual review found no prompt injection, exfiltration, dynamic shell execution, or malicious network behavior in the cited files. Most static findings are Markdown documentation false positives, but the skill intentionally creates persistent subagent files and manages tool permissions.

remediation.issue: Generated subagents can change future Claude Code behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Require user review before saving or activating files under `.claude/agents`, especially descriptions and system prompts.

remediation.issue: Tool permissions can become broader than needed.
remediation.suggestion: Always emit an explicit minimal `tools` field and avoid inherited all-tool defaults.
Prefer project-level `.claude/agents` paths unless the user explicitly asks for a user-level agent.

content.value_statement: Building Claude Code subagents requires consistent structure, clear scope, and careful tool permissions. This skill guides agent design, updates, validation, and placement in the correct `.claude/agents` folder.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes requirements to identify a focused subagent role.
Chooses a model tier based on task complexity.
Selects minimal tool permissions for each subagent.
Builds YAML frontmatter for name, description, tools, model, and color.
Uses a standard template for responsibilities, workflow, rules, and acceptance criteria.
Reports the created or updated agent path and usage guidance.
limitations: It cannot verify runtime behavior after a subagent is activated.
It depends on the user to approve filesystem changes.
It does not replace a security review of generated prompts.
It is focused on Claude Code subagents, not general agent frameworks.

use_cases.title: Create a focused reviewer
use_cases.description: Define a code review subagent with scoped read tools, clear priorities, and concise reporting.

use_cases.title: Update an existing workflow agent
use_cases.description: Revise a team subagent with new responsibilities, model selection, and updated acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Standardize agent configuration
use_cases.description: Apply one template across project agents so permissions, rules, and outputs stay consistent.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic subagent
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Code subagent for [task]. Include purpose, tools, model tier, workflow, constraints, and acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Update an existing subagent
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the [agent-name] subagent for [new requirement]. Preserve its main role and adjust tools, workflow, and acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Design a team agent set
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these development workflows: [workflow list]. Propose specialized Claude Code subagents with names, scopes, tools, and model tiers.

prompt_templates.title: Harden permissions
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this subagent configuration: [agent details]. Reduce tool permissions, remove overlapping duties, and tighten rules without losing required capabilities.

output_examples.input: Create a subagent for automated test analysis.
output: A focused test-analysis role with a concise purpose.
A minimal tool set for reading files, searching code, and running tests.
A workflow covering assessment, execution, failure triage, and reporting.
A saved agent path and activation guidance.

output_examples.input: Update the code-reviewer subagent for security checks.
output: A revised reviewer scope that includes security review.
Tighter rules for secrets, input validation, and risky permissions.
Updated acceptance criteria for findings and remediation guidance.

output_examples.input: Design agents for a product engineering team.
output: A small set of specialized agent roles.
Recommended model tiers for each role.
Tool permission guidance for each agent.
Notes about role overlap and maintenance.

best_practices: Review generated subagent files before enabling them in Claude Code.
Grant only the tools each subagent needs for its defined role.
Keep each subagent focused on one responsibility area.
anti_patterns: Creating broad agents that duplicate existing roles.
Omitting the tools field when the subagent needs limited access.
Saving user-level agents when project-level scope is enough.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates or updates Claude Code subagent Markdown files with YAML frontmatter and structured instructions.

faq.question: Does it run generated agents?
faq.answer: No. It designs and saves configurations, then reports the file path and usage guidance.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: It is documented for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code marketplace compatibility.

faq.question: Can it update an existing subagent?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks whether the agent exists, then revises scope, tools, model tier, and acceptance criteria.

faq.question: How should permissions be handled?
faq.answer: Use the smallest explicit tool list that supports the subagent role.

faq.question: Where are agent files saved?
faq.answer: The skill targets project `.claude/agents` folders and team subfolders unless another scope is requested.
